newsitem.title: USA: President Clinton commits to democracy in D.C..
newsitem.headline: President Clinton commits to democracy in D.C..

text.p: President Clinton Monday pledged to help the District of Columbia regain the right to rule itself after Congress last week suspended the powers of local elected officials.

"The president was clear that he will help me in whatever way we can to begin the process of getting back the Home Rule we lost," D.C. Congressional delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton told reporters after talks with Clinton at the White House.

Lawmakers have passed legislation that suspends the right of the city's government to collect taxes, pave roads and educate their children in return for a multi-billion dollar federal bailout for the cash-starved nation's capital.
"We, in our meeting today, all agreed to try to march ahead to undo that damage," Norton said.
The law turned over most decision making about the day-to-day running of the city to a five-member control board created by Congress two years ago at the height of the District's insolvency.

In return, the bankrupt city gets billions of dollars in federal aid to pay worker pensions, health care costs and other bills it inherited in 1974 when it won from Congress the right to elect a mayor and govern itself.
But city leaders, including Mayor Marion Barry and Norton, D.C.'s only delegate to Capitol Hill, are enraged by a provision in the law taking away their vote on key decisions.
Norton, who says she was betrayed by last-minute changes to the legislation, requested the meeting with Clinton.
Last week, dozens of angry protestors shouted "treason" as the control board held its first meeting since the law was passed and a bomb threat finally ended the stormy session.
